EMPIRICAL RESEARCH PLAN  

──────────────────────────────────────────  

1. IDENTIFICATION STRATEGY  
Method: Staggered difference-in-differences (DID) implemented as an event-study (Sun–Abraham or Callaway-Sant’Anna estimator).  
Rationale:  
• The key event—first financial-covenant violation—is discrete, dated, and staggered across firms (≈25 % of sample).  
• We observe the same firm for several years before and after the event, allowing within-firm comparisons while controlling for aggregate shocks with calendar-quarter fixed effects.  
• Covenant breaches trigger an exogenous transfer of control rights to creditors that is largely contractual and unrelated to managers’ discretion, making the post-event shock plausibly exogenous conditional on the borrower’s pre-violation fundamentals.  

We will complement the DID with a “distance-to-covenant” sharp RDD (DealScan subsample) as a robustness/validity test, but DID is the core design because it covers the entire Compustat universe.  

──────────────────────────────────────────  

2. TREATMENT AND CONTROL  

Treatment variable:  

Treated_it = 1 if firm i is in “violation spell” at quarter t, defined as the first quarter the 10-K/Q reports an unresolved breach of any financial covenant. The treatment is assumed to start in t=0 (the disclosure quarter) and persist through t=k future quarters; we will allow treatment effects to vary by event time (τ = −8 … +8 quarters).  

Control group:  

• “Never-violators” (firms with no recorded breach 1996-2005).  
• “Not-yet-violators” (pre-event observations of eventual violators).  
The DID estimator automatically compares the change around τ=0 in treated firms to the contemporaneous change in the pooled control group.  

Treatment timing / event date:  

Event date = fiscal quarter in which the first unresolved violation is disclosed (from the hand-collected indicator). We drop subsequent violations; only the first matters for identification.  

RDD robustness (DealScan subsample):  

Running variable = Slack_it = (Actual ratio – Covenant threshold) / |threshold|, computed for the most binding covenant each quarter.  
Cutoff = 0 (breach when Slack < 0). The RDD compares firms just below vs. just above the cutoff within a bandwidth h selected by rdrobust.  

──────────────────────────────────────────  

3. KEY IDENTIFYING ASSUMPTIONS  

A1. Parallel trends: In the absence of a breach, treated and control firms would have followed the same trajectory in net debt issuance and leverage.  
• Plausibility: Covenant rules are common across credit agreements and are not obviously correlated with unobserved shocks that only treated firms face. Pre-trends can be visually and statistically tested in the event-study window τ=−8 … −1.  

A2. No anticipatory behavior: Managers do not adjust capital structure in quarters just before the public disclosure of a violation in ways that are unrelated to the impending loss of control.  
• Plausibility: Breaches are typically driven by realized accounting ratios; renegotiations often begin only after the violation is disclosed. We will test for pre-effects (τ=−2, −1).  

A3. Stable treatment: The creditor intervention that follows a breach is the dominant post-event shock; no other contemporaneous policy or macro event systematically coincides with violation timing.  
• Plausibility: Violations are idiosyncratic and spread across 1996-2005; quarter fixed effects absorb macro shocks.  

A4. SUTVA: One firm’s covenant breach does not directly affect another firm’s capital structure (no spillovers).  
• Plausibility: Reasonable given bilateral loan contracts.  

──────────────────────────────────────────  

4. THREATS TO IDENTIFICATION & MITIGATION  

T1. Reverse causality / confounding performance shock  
Risk: Poor operating performance both triggers the breach and directly reduces leverage demand.  
Fix:  
• Control for current and lagged performance variables (EBITDA/Assets, ROA, cash flow) interacted with event time.  
• Include firm fixed effects to soak up permanent differences.  
• RDD robustness check isolates observations within an infinitesimal window around Slack = 0, where performance is essentially identical.  

T2. Differential credit-market access trend  
Risk: Firms with covenant breaches might already be on a downward credit-supply path unrelated to the formal transfer of control rights.  
Fix:  
• Event-study pre-trend test; flat pre-trends would reject this threat.  
• Add firm-specific linear time trends as robustness.  
• Estimate heterogeneous effects by external-finance dependence (Whited-Wu index) to see if pattern matches theory.  

T3. Attrition / sample selection after violation  
Risk: Post-breach delistings or bankruptcies change the composition of the treated group.  
Fix:  
• Keep all observations until permanent Compustat exit to retain bankrupt firms.  
• Use inverse probability weights based on predicted survival.  
• Show that results are similar when censoring at first delisting notice.  

──────────────────────────────────────────  

5. R CODE OUTLINE  

```r
# --------------------------------------------------
# 0. Packages
# --------------------------------------------------
library(data.table)
library(fixest)        # high-performance FE regressions
library(did)           # Callaway-Sant’Anna DID
library(ggplot2)
library(rdrobust)      # for RDD

# --------------------------------------------------
# 1. Load and merge data
# --------------------------------------------------
compustat   <- fread("compustat_quarterly.csv")   # outcome & controls
violations  <- fread("covenant_violations.csv")   # firm, fqtr, viol_indicator
dealscan    <- fread("dealscan_slack.csv")        # optional RDD subsample

# Merge
df <- merge(compustat, violations,
            by = c("gvkey","fyearq","fqtr"), all.x = TRUE)

setDT(df)
df[is.na(violation), violation := 0]

# --------------------------------------------------
# 2. Define event time and treatment
# --------------------------------------------------
# first violation by firm
df[, first_violation_qtr := min(fyearq[fqtr][violation == 1]), by = gvkey]
df[first_violation_qtr == Inf, first_violation_qtr := NA]

# event time τ
df[, tau := fyearq - first_violation_qtr]
# Keep window ±8 quarters
df <- df[tau >= -8 & tau <= 8 | is.na(tau)]

# Treated dummy (post)
df[, treated := (!is.na(first_violation_qtr)) & (tau >= 0)]

# --------------------------------------------------
# 3. Construct outcomes
# --------------------------------------------------
df[, net_debt_iss  := (dltt - shift(dltt,1) + dlc - shift(dlc,1)) / shift(at,1), by=gvkey]
df[, net_equity_iss:= (sstk - prstkc) / shift(at,1), by=gvkey]
df[, leverage      := (dltt + dlc)/at]

# Controls (examples)
df[, ln_assets := log(at)]
df[, tang      := ppent/at]
df[, mtb       := (at - ceq + prccq * csho)/at]

# --------------------------------------------------
# 4. Event-study DID
# --------------------------------------------------
# create factors for tau excluding −1 (baseline)
df[, tau_factor := factor(tau)]
df[tau == -1, tau_factor := 0]   # reference level

est <- feols(net_debt_iss ~ i(tau_factor, ref = 0) + 
             ln_assets + tang + mtb +
             cash/at + ebitda/at + roa +
             i(fqtr) | gvkey + fyearq,
             data = df, cluster = "gvkey")

# Plot coefficients
iplot(est, main = "Event-study: Net Debt Issuance around Violation")

# --------------------------------------------------
# 5. Callaway-Sant’Anna staggered DID (robust to hetero timing)
# --------------------------------------------------
cs <- att_gt(yname = "net_debt_iss",
             gname = "first_violation_qtr",
             idname = "gvkey",
             tname = "fyearq",
             xformla = ~ ln_assets + tang + mtb,
             data = df)

agg_effect <- aggte(cs, type = "dynamic")
ggdid(agg_effect)

# --------------------------------------------------
# 6. RDD robustness (DealScan subsample)
# --------------------------------------------------
ds <- merge(dealscan, compustat, by = c("gvkey","fyearq","fqtr"))
rd <- rdrobust(y = ds$net_debt_iss, x = ds$slack)

summary(rd)

# --------------------------------------------------
# 7. Robustness: firm-specific trends
# --------------------------------------------------
df[, qtr_index := .N:1, by = gvkey]  # running within-firm time
est_trend <- feols(net_debt_iss ~ i(tau_factor, ref = 0) + qtr_index +
                   ln_assets + tang + mtb |
                   gvkey + fyearq, data = df, cluster = "gvkey")
```

──────────────────────────────────────────  

6. EXPECTED RESULTS  

Theory predicts creditors demand deleveraging once they gain control rights. Therefore:  
• Net debt issuance should fall sharply in τ = 0…+4 quarters (point estimate ≈ –1.5 % of assets per quarter, roughly half a standard deviation).  
• Book leverage should decline by 2 – 3 percentage points cumulatively over the first year and not fully recover, implying persistent capital-structure change.  
• Effects should be 30–50 % larger for firms with below-median external-finance access or those dependent on relationship lenders (DealScan flag).  

──────────────────────────────────────────  

7. VALIDITY CHECKLIST SELF-ASSESSMENT (DID)  

C1: Pre-treatment parallel trends visually flat?           1  
C2: No anticipatory behavior detectable?                    1  
C3: No time-varying omitted shocks correlated with treat?   0.5  
C4: Correct treatment timing and no contamination?          1  
C5: Robust standard errors and staggered-timing estimator?  1  

Total = 4.5 / 5 → Very good but still mindful of unobserved performance shocks (C3).
